place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 正殿前 · 大比擂台
place.en: Chending Temple · Before the main hall · the contest platform

setup.zh: 外门大比。名册上三百多个名字，大半弃了权，剩下六十几个人上台；人人都押马小宝——他练气五层了，马家为了这一枚筑基丹，把蒙山上的树卖了三成。
setup.en: The outer court contest. Three hundred-odd names are on the register, most have withdrawn, sixty-some will fight — and everyone is betting on Ma Xiaobao — he is at layer five now, and the Ma family sold three-tenths of the trees on Mount Meng for this one Foundation pill.

recap.zh: 腊月初八，外门大比开场：所有人都押马小宝。抽签，你对孙二狗。
recap.en: The eighth of the twelfth month, the contest opens: everyone backs Ma Xiaobao. The lots: you against Sun Ergou.

zh: 头名，筑基丹一枚。整个沉鼎观，只一枚。
en: The eighth of the twelfth month: the outer court contest.
First place: one Foundation pill. The only one the temple has.
Everyone is betting on Ma Xiaobao.

story.zh:
大比的台子搭在外门的演武场上，叫作五行台——其实是五块青石板拼成的一个圆，年头久了，缝里都长出了草，也不知道当初为什么起这么大一个名字。周衡说，大约是祖师起的；祖师起名字，向来是往大了起的，譬如沉鼎观，观里并没有鼎；譬如五行台，台上也并没有五行，只有五块石头。他说这话的时候，正蹲在台子边上拿一本账簿记今天搭台用了多少根绳子，记完了，合上账簿，补了一句：「有前途。」也不知是说台子，还是说绳子。

外门大比，向来是一日打完的。名册上三百多个名字，真上台的却没有这许多：入门头一年的、练气不到三层的、跟阿禾一样把账算过一遍的，大半都在自己名字后头画了圈，执事念弃权的名单，念了足足一炷香，末了剩下六十几个人。六十几个人，捉对厮杀，输一场便下去，一轮刷掉一半，打到天黑，恰好剩下一个。一场只给半炷香，半炷香里分不出胜负，执事便看谁站得离台心近，谁近谁赢——这条规矩是哪一年定的，周衡的账上也查不着，只知道自打有了它，外门弟子比武，十个里倒有八个是往台心挤，挤得跟过年抢头香一般。

抽签是在台前一只大竹筒里抽的。六十几根竹签，一根一根抽出来，执事念一个名字，台下便嗡的一声。念到马小宝的时候，嗡声最大，马小宝的两个跟班扯着嗓子叫好，叫得远处山门上的乌鸦都飞起来了。马小宝站在人群当中，穿一身簇新的法衣，腰里挂着一面巴掌大的铜镜，脸上一片一片的斑，红的紫的，像是一块没擦干净的灶台。这是他家这三个月一车一车往山上送丹药，硬喂出来的：练气五层，丹斑也五层。据说马家老爷为了这一颗筑基丹，把蒙山上的树卖了三成，那三成树砍下来，顺着泗水往下游漂，漂了半个月还没漂完。

小满站在人群后头，听见有人这么说，心里一动。他想起他爹说过的话：前山被马家篦了一遍又一遍。篦完了野兽，又篦树。他又想起小时候村里孩子们排成一串、扮九头蛇时唱的那支歌，一个头，吃一山，两个头，吃两川。他摇了摇头，把这支歌甩出去，心想：马家又不是九头蛇，马家只有一个头，马三那个头，又宽又圆，像一扇门。

抽签的时候，周衡坐在竹筒旁边，一个名字一个名字往大比的名录上誊。那名录是一本老账簿，蓝布面，边角都给翻烂了，前头几十页记的是历年的大比，一年一页，一页上头一行，写的是那一年的头名。小满排队抽签，排到周衡跟前，瞧见那名录正翻在前头，一页一页，墨色从新到旧，旧到后来，黄得像秋天的树叶。有一页上，头名那一行的名字给人拿笔划了一道，划得很直，划过去的墨比字的墨还新些，底下的名字给水渍洇开了，看不清写的是什么。

小满问道：「周师兄，这一个怎么划了？」

周衡头也不抬，道：「划了的，是不在观里了的。」

小满道：「死了？」

周衡道：「不在观里了。」他把名录往后一翻，翻到今年那一页，蘸了蘸墨，「账上只记在不在，不记为什么。为什么，不归我管。」说罢冲他一伸手，「签。」

小满便把手伸进竹筒里。

签抽到他了。执事念道：「沈小满——对，孙二狗。」

台下有人笑出了声。
story.en:
The contest stage was set up on the outer court's training ground and was called the Five Elements Platform — in fact five bluestone slabs laid in a circle, so old that grass grew in the seams, and who knows why it was ever given so grand a name. Zhou Heng said it was probably the founder; the founder always named things big — Chending Temple, for instance, with no cauldron in it; the Five Elements Platform, with no five elements on it, only five stones. He said this squatting at the edge of the stage, entering in a ledger how many lengths of rope had gone into building it; when he'd finished he closed the ledger and added, "Promising." Whether he meant the stage or the rope, nobody knew.

The outer court contest was always fought in a single day. Three hundred-odd names were on the register, but far fewer took the stage: first-years, those below the third level of Qi Refining, those who had done the sums as A He had — most had circled their own names, and the steward read out the withdrawals for a full stick of incense, leaving sixty-some. Sixty-some, paired off, one loss and you're out, half gone each round, and by nightfall exactly one left. Each bout got half a stick of incense; if no one won in that time, the steward looked at who stood nearer the centre, and nearer won — which year that rule was made, even Zhou Heng's ledgers couldn't say; only that ever since, eight outer disciples in ten, when they fought, crowded for the centre like a New Year's scramble for the first incense.

Lots were drawn from a big bamboo tube in front of the stage. Sixty-some bamboo slips, drawn one by one; each time the steward read a name, the crowd below hummed. At Ma Xiaobao's name the hum was loudest; his two followers bawled their approval till the crows on the gate far off took wing. Ma Xiaobao stood in the middle of the crowd in a brand-new robe, a palm-sized bronze mirror at his waist, his face blotched red and purple like a stove top not wiped clean. That was what three months of pills sent up the mountain by the cartload, forced down him, had made: the fifth level of Qi Refining, and five levels of pill blotches. Word was that for this one Foundation pill old master Ma had sold three-tenths of the trees on Meng Mountain; felled, they floated down the Si for half a month and still hadn't all gone by.

Standing at the back of the crowd, hearing someone say this, Xiaoman's heart stirred. He remembered his father saying the Ma family had combed the front hills again and again. Combed out the game, then combed the trees. And he remembered the song the village children sang lined up in a chain, playing the nine-headed snake: one head eats a mountain, two heads eat two rivers. He shook his head and threw the song out, thinking: the Ma family's no nine-headed snake; the Ma family has only one head, and Ma San's head, wide and round, is like a door.

While lots were drawn, Zhou Heng sat by the tube copying names one by one into the contest register. The register was an old ledger, blue cloth covers, its corners worn to rags; the first few dozen pages recorded past contests, a year to a page, and the top line of each page the first place of that year. Queuing to draw, Xiaoman reached Zhou Heng just as the register lay open near the front; page after page, the ink going from new to old, old till it was yellow as autumn leaves. On one page the name on the first-place line had been struck through with a single stroke of the brush, very straight, the ink of the stroke newer than the name's; beneath it the name had blurred in a water stain, past reading.

"Brother Zhou," asked Xiaoman, "why is this one struck out?"

Zhou Heng didn't look up. "The ones struck out are the ones no longer at the temple."

"Dead?"

"No longer at the temple." He turned to this year's page and dipped his brush. "The books record whether you're here, not why. Why isn't mine to see to." And he held out a hand. "Your slip."

So Xiaoman put his hand in the tube.

The slip was drawn. The steward read out: "Shen Xiaoman — against Sun Ergou."

Someone below laughed out loud.

exits.means: steps up onto the contest platform for the first round
